title: Eid al-Fitr: the takbir
hookLine: on the way to Eid prayer, Allah is greatest, sung aloud

lines: NEW SHOES, DATES AT THE DOOR.
ONE PHRASE, SUNG IN THE STREET.
cards: The crescent moon has been sighted, or the announcement has come through. Ramadan is over. The next morning, early, families are up in their best clothes.
Kids in new shoes. Someone is handing out dates at the door.

And from the mosque, from the open field where the prayer will be held, from people walking down the street in twos and threes, comes one phrase, sung over and over, in a melody many Muslims learned as children: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar.
Today, the sound of Eid morning.

teach.b: The phrase is the takbir, from the root k-b-r, to be great. Allahu akbar: God is greater, God is greatest. Takbirat is the plural: the takbirs.
On Eid al-Fitr, they fill the morning. Many scholars connect the practice with the end of the very verse from three days ago about Ramadan.
It closes by saying God wants ease for you, and wants you to complete the count of days, and in Pickthall's words, "that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you".
Magnify, there, is the same verb, tukabbiru: to say God is great. So the fast ends, the count is complete, and the first thing to do is the takbir.
A common form goes: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar, Allahu akbar, wa lillahil hamd.

God is greatest, God is greatest, there is no god but God, God is greatest, God is greatest, and to God belongs all praise. The wording and the number of repetitions vary a little between schools and regions.
Then come small things the hadith preserve.
Bukhari reports that the Prophet ﷺ wouldn't go out on the morning of Eid al-Fitr until he'd eaten some dates, an odd number of them.
He went to the prayer by one road and came back by another; scholars give several reasons, and a common one is that more people would see and greet him.
The charity of the fast, zakat al-fitr, was to be given before the prayer, so the poor could celebrate too.
And in the Eid prayer itself there are extra takbirs, in many schools with raised hands, their number differing between schools. A month of quiet effort ends out loud.

how: On Eid al-Fitr, Muslims give zakat al-fitr before the prayer, often eat a few dates, and recite the takbir aloud on the way to the congregational Eid prayer, which includes extra takbirs; the wording and count vary by school.

practice: If you pray, say the takbir quietly, in Arabic or English, a few times through, and let it grow a little stronger each time.
If you don't, picture the street on Eid morning: the clothes, the dates, the voices, the crowd heading the same way.
